as_told.title: Urartian cuneiform inscriptions misattribute the ruins

plain: Archaeologists credit the ruins, carvings and symbols around Lake Van in Turkey to the Urartians, a people of the region roughly 3,000 years ago, because they carved cuneiform, an ancient wedge-shaped script, into some of the temples. The researcher Matt LaCroix says on Michels's show that he believes the Urartians were a later people who built on top of much older work. If true, an older and unknown culture would have built the original sites.
